title: Master’s Of Magicka · mom-bot Guide
audience: Master’s Of Magicka officers · Sign-in required
intro: Use this officer reference to manage mom-bot’s extra Discord features and help clanmates use their preference buttons. Website planning and the core bot’s assignment messages are covered in the General Usage Guide.

sections.title: 1. Find and run a Discord command
sections.summary: Use mom-bot inside the Master’s Of Magicka server and select its command from Discord’s suggestions.

tasks.title: Run a slash command
steps: Open the **Master’s Of Magicka** Discord server, then a channel where bot commands are allowed. Ask the coordinating officer which channel to use if necessary.
Click or tap the message box and type **/** followed by the command name. Select the command belonging to **mom-bot** from the suggestions.
If the command has fields, fill them using Discord’s choices or member picker. Send it with Enter on a computer or the send control on a phone.
Read the bot’s reply. A command sent as plain text, rather than selected from the command suggestions, may not run.
tasks.note: A slash command is a request to the bot. Use these commands inside the clan server. Officer reminder and join-alert commands require Discord’s **Manage Server** permission; a website planning role does not automatically grant that Discord permission.

tasks.title: Check whether mom-bot responds
steps: Select **/ping** from mom-bot’s command suggestions and send it.
Look for the response showing the running version and uptime, meaning how long the bot has been running.
tasks.note: A successful ping shows that the bot can answer. If a preference or reminder command still fails, report the specific failing command rather than assuming every feature is working.

sections.title: 2. Help members choose post preferences
sections.summary: The member commands edit the caller’s own preferences. Use the website to review another member’s record.

tasks.title: Show the available conditions and saved choices
paragraphs: **/post-conditions** displays the complete condition catalog, grouped into categories.
**/post-conditions-get** displays the preferences saved for the person who ran it. If it says no preferences are set, use the set command below.
Preference command replies are visible only to the caller in Discord. Saved preferences are used by the website for clan siege planning.

tasks.title: Choose, save, and verify preferences
steps: Have the member select and send **/post-conditions-set**. An editor opens with their existing selections.
Tap a condition button to select it. Selected buttons turn green; tapping again removes that choice. Select the restrictions their actual teams can handle.
Use **Next ▶** and **◀ Prev** to move through the pages. Choices stay selected as the member changes pages.
Read the selected-preferences summary, then choose **Save**. Wait for **Preferences saved** before leaving.
Run **/post-conditions-get** to verify what was stored.
tasks.result: The member’s saved website preferences reflect the selected conditions. Existing siege placements are not automatically moved.
tasks.note: **Cancel** preserves the previous saved choices. The editor is available for about five minutes. If buttons expire or stop responding, open a fresh editor with /post-conditions-set, check the selections, and save again.

tasks.title: Correct an unregistered or mismatched account
steps: If the bot says the account is not registered, ask which Discord account the member used to run the command.
On the website, open **Members** and find that person’s record. Check their Discord username and use **Sync Discord → Fetch Preview** to review the account match.
Correct only matches you can verify, then apply the selected match. Ask the member to run their preference command again.
tasks.note: The bot preference commands have no target-member field or officer override. They act on the caller’s account. Use the website’s member page and **Save Preferences** when an officer needs to edit another member’s preferences.

sections.title: 3. Understand scheduled clan reminders
sections.summary: Read recurring event notices and distinguish channel reminders from personal assignment messages.

tasks.title: Read the latest event notice
paragraphs: Mom-bot can post Hydra, Chimera, Siege, and Hydra Tank Week reminders in the clan’s Discord channels. Read the latest message’s date and instructions before acting.
These scheduled channel notices differ from the website’s **Notify Members** assignment DMs and the recurring personal reminders managed below.
If an event notice appears to use the wrong date, channel, or schedule, tell the bot maintainer which notice needs checking. The supported officer commands below manage recurring member DMs.

tasks.title: Investigate a missing personal message
steps: Ask the member to check message requests and allow direct messages from members of the clan server in Discord’s server privacy settings.
Check whether the member has blocked mom-bot and whether the intended reminder names the correct account.

For website-generated assignments, use the siege’s **Settings → Discord Notifications** results to check the delivery batch. For recurring personal reminders, inspect the reminder with /member-notify-get.

sections.title: 4. Create a recurring personal reminder
sections.summary: Choose one member, a unique reminder name, a start date, a time, and a repeat interval.

tasks.title: Fill in /member-notify-add
steps: Select **/member-notify-add** from mom-bot’s suggestions. If the command is missing, check that you have Discord’s **Manage Server** permission.
In **member**, use Discord’s member picker to choose the recipient. Check the actual account before proceeding.
In **name**, enter a unique label you can recognize later, such as **weekly-hydra-alex**. In **message**, enter the exact reminder the member should receive.

Enter **start_date** as year-month-day, for example **2026-11-05**. Enter **time** as a 24-hour **UTC** time, for example **18:30**. These fields use UTC, not your device’s local timezone; check the conversion before sending.
Choose **cadence**: **Weekly** repeats every 7 days; **Biweekly** repeats every 14 days; **Monthly** repeats on the start date’s day of the month.
Send the command and read the confirmation. Use **/member-notify-get** with the same name to review the saved details.
tasks.note: For a monthly reminder on a day that does not exist in a shorter month, the reminder falls on that month’s last day. UTC stays fixed when local daylight-saving time changes, so recheck the local time if that matters to the member.

tasks.title: Resolve an input error
paragraphs: If the name already exists, inspect it with **/member-notify-get** before creating another. Use a different label only if you want a separate reminder.
For a date error, use a real date in year-month-day form. For a time error, use hour:minute in 24-hour form, with hours 00–23 and minutes 00–59.
A successful creation confirmation means the reminder was saved. It does not mean its first scheduled DM has already been delivered.

sections.title: 5. Find, change, pause, or remove reminders
sections.summary: Use the reminder’s unique name to manage it without creating duplicates.

tasks.title: Find and inspect a reminder
steps: Run **/member-notify-list** to find the existing names.
Run **/member-notify-get** and supply the exact **name** to inspect the recipient, message, schedule, and enabled state.
Check that you have the right reminder before changing or deleting it.

tasks.title: Change the recipient, message, or schedule
steps: Select **/member-notify-update** and enter the existing reminder’s **name**.
Supply the fields you want to change: member, message, start_date, time, or cadence. Recheck UTC when changing the date or time.
Send the command, read the result, then use **/member-notify-get** to verify the new details.

tasks.title: Pause and resume a reminder
steps: Choose **/member-notify-update**, supply the reminder’s **name**, and set **enabled** to **False** to pause it.
Check the saved enabled state with **/member-notify-get**.
To resume it, run update for the same name with **enabled: True**. Check the schedule as well before resuming.
tasks.result: The reminder record is retained so it can be resumed instead of recreated.

tasks.title: Remove a reminder permanently
steps: Inspect the reminder first with **/member-notify-get** and confirm the exact name.
Select **/member-notify-remove**, supply that name, and send it only if the reminder should be deleted.
Check the result and use **/member-notify-list** to confirm that the reminder is gone.
tasks.note: Use pause instead if you may want the same reminder again. The remove command deletes the named reminder rather than temporarily disabling it.

sections.title: 6. Subscribe to new-member join alerts
sections.summary: Choose whether you personally receive an officer DM when someone joins the server.

tasks.title: Turn your alerts on or off
steps: Select **/notify-new-members** and choose **state: On** to receive join-alert DMs.
Send the command and check the confirmation. Make sure your Discord privacy settings allow the bot’s messages.
To stop your alerts, run the same command with **state: Off**.
tasks.note: This changes the invoking officer’s subscription, not everybody’s alerts. The command requires Discord’s Manage Server permission. Mom-bot also handles welcome and follow-up messages as configured for the clan.

sections.title: 7. Check siege-day roles
sections.summary: Understand how website attack-day choices can update Discord roles.

tasks.title: Investigate a mismatched Day 1 or Day 2 label
steps: Check the member’s **Attack Day** in the correct siege’s **Members** tab. Confirm the date and account match first.
If the plan itself is wrong and still editable, correct the attack day through the website and check the saved result.

Where day-role synchronization is enabled, check the corresponding Discord role afterward. If it disagrees with the saved plan, report the member, date, intended day, and observed role to the bot maintainer.
tasks.note: A Discord role is a label on a member’s account. Do not change another part of the siege plan just to work around a role-sync problem. Resolve a locked plan through the clan’s planning process.

sections.title: 8. Troubleshoot a command
sections.summary: Check the server, account, permission, saved result, and visible error before escalating.

tasks.title: The command is missing or unavailable
paragraphs: Use the Master’s Of Magicka server and an allowed channel, then select the command belonging to mom-bot from Discord’s slash suggestions.
Check Manage Server permission for member-notification and join-alert commands. A strength role such as Heavy Hitter is unrelated to Discord command permission.
If a member preference command is missing, ask the bot maintainer to check command availability in that channel.

tasks.title: The bot returned an error or stopped responding
steps: For expired preference buttons, open a fresh /post-conditions-set editor and verify the saved result with /post-conditions-get.
For another command error, read the visible reply and correct any named input problem. If it appears temporary, try again after a short wait.
If it continues, tell the bot maintainer the command, when it ran, and what the reply said. Include the reminder name or siege date when relevant.
tasks.note: Do not repeatedly create reminders or send assignment batches while a result is uncertain. Inspect the existing record or delivery result first so members do not receive duplicates.
